title: Suffering from disease and aging, And also subject to death — Such is the nature of conditioned things, Such is the nature of beings. If…
content:
Suffering from disease and aging,
And also subject to death —
Such is the nature of conditioned things,
Such is the nature of beings.
If ordinary people become disenchanted,
That would not be fitting for me —
If I too were disenchanted
With beings who share the same fate.
While I live,
Not different from them,
I dwell thus,
Knowing the Dhamma without attachment.
Conceit in health,
In youth, in life —
All these I have subdued,
Springing from security.
I see the path of seclusion,
I arouse strong energy,
Seeing the state of Nibbāna.
Now I cannot
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
I will not fall back,
Achieving the final goal of the holy life.

title: Who once was heedless, but later is not, Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds. Whoever stops an evil deed by a wholesome…
content:
Who once was heedless, but later is not,
Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds.
Whoever stops an evil deed by a wholesome one,
Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds.

title: Elder Māluṅkyaputta: One who lives heedlessly, Craving grows like a creeper. He drifts and wanders, Life after life, Like a monkey in the forest, Longing…
content:
Elder Māluṅkyaputta:

One who lives heedlessly,
Craving grows like a creeper.
He drifts and wanders,
Life after life,
Like a monkey in the forest,
Longing for fruit.

This wretched craving
Poisons the whole world.
When it conquers anyone,
Sorrow increases —
Like birana grass
Spreading and growing.

One who subdues craving,
Wretched, hard to conquer —
Sorrow falls from that person
Like a water drop from a lotus.

You have come here —
I teach this good thing.
Dig up the root of craving
Like seeking the sweet root
Of the usīra grass.
Do not let Māra, the flood,
Destroy you like a reed,
Again and again, forever.

Practice the Buddha’s instruction.
Do not let the moment pass.
If the moment passes, sorrow,
You will suffer in hell.

Heedlessness is dust,
Filthy dust born of heedlessness.
Heedful, with clear wisdom,
Pull out the dart from yourself.

title: One whose mind inclines to renunciation, His heart tends toward seclusion; One whose mind inclines to non-ill-will, His heart tends toward the cessation of clinging;…
content:
One whose mind inclines to renunciation,
His heart tends toward seclusion;
One whose mind inclines to non-ill-will,
His heart tends toward the cessation of clinging;
One whose mind inclines to the cessation of craving,
His heart tends toward the absence of delusion;
Seeing the place of arising,
His mind is rightly liberated.
For one rightly liberated,
The monk with a pure mind,
There is nothing further to do,
Nothing remains to be done.
Like a solid mass of rock,
Unmoved by the wind,
So too, all forms,
Tastes, sounds, smells, contacts,
And all phenomena —
Agreeable or disagreeable —
Cannot disturb one such as this,
Whose mind is steady, liberated,
Seeing the nature of their cessation.

title: “Ānanda, I do not see any form where delight and pleasure are subject to change, alteration, and do not give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain,…
content: “Ānanda, I do not see any form where delight and pleasure are subject to change, alteration, and do not give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.”

title: “From attachment arises grief, From attachment arises fear. For one freed from attachment, No grief, no fear.” “From delight arises grief, From delight arises fear.…
content:
“From attachment arises grief,
From attachment arises fear.
For one freed from attachment,
No grief, no fear.”

“From delight arises grief,
From delight arises fear.
For one freed from delight,
No grief, no fear.”

“From sensual desire arises grief,
From sensual desire arises fear.
For one freed from sensual desire,
No grief, no fear.”

“From craving arises grief,
From craving arises fear.
For one freed from craving,
No grief, no fear.”

title: “Monks, just as in a dense forest there is a large deep lake, and a great herd of deer lives near one side. Then a…
content: “Monks, just as in a dense forest there is a large deep lake, and a great herd of deer lives near one side. Then a man comes who does not desire their welfare, does not desire their benefit, does not desire their security from bondage. He closes off the safe, secure path leading to happiness and opens a dangerous path, sets a male decoy and a female decoy. Monks, then that great herd of deer will later fall into bondage and decline. Monks, then a man comes who desires their welfare, desires their benefit, desires their security from bondage. He opens the safe, secure path, closes the dangerous path, removes the male decoy, and destroys the female decoy. Monks, then that great herd of deer will later increase, prosper, and become abundant.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen wholesome states arise and arisen unwholesome states decline, as fewness of wishes. For one…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen wholesome states arise and arisen unwholesome states decline, as fewness of wishes. For one with few wishes, monks, unarisen wholesome states arise and arisen unwholesome states decline.”

title: Do not pursue the past, Do not long for the future. The past is left behind, The future has not yet come. Only the present…
content:
Do not pursue the past,
Do not long for the future.
The past is left behind,
The future has not yet come.
Only the present Dhamma —
See it clearly here and now.
Unmoved, unshaken —
Knowing this, cultivate it.
Make an effort today —
Who knows death tomorrow?
No one can negotiate
With the great army of Death.
Living thus ardently,
Both day and night untiring —
That is called the Sage of the One Night,
The peaceful, the calm.

title: “Monks, with guarded faculties, with completeness in guarding the faculties, virtue is complete. With virtue present, with completeness in virtue, right concentration is complete. With…
content: “Monks, with guarded faculties, with completeness in guarding the faculties, virtue is complete. With virtue present, with completeness in virtue, right concentration is complete. With right concentration present, with completeness in right concentration, true knowledge and vision are complete. With true knowledge and vision present, with completeness in true knowledge and vision, disenchantment and dispassion are complete. With disenchantment and dispassion present, with completeness in disenchantment and dispassion, the knowledge and vision of liberation are complete. Just as, monks, a tree with complete branches and foliage — its shoots reach perfection, its bark reaches perfection, its sapwood reaches perfection, its heartwood reaches perfection. So too, monks, with guarded faculties, with completeness in guarding the faculties … the knowledge and vision of liberation are complete.”
